cars.generation: Original SS Jaguar 100 overhead-valve sports roadster
cars.variant: SS Jaguar 100 2½ Litre — 1938 heritage road reference
cars.specification_market: Jaguar Daimler Heritage Trust collection account: selected 1938 2½ Litre road reference ERB 290, chassis 49033, built January 20, 1938. The 2½ Litre designation is nominal, not a claim of exactly 2500 cc. Source background specifications describe the original 102-bhp version, not a measurement of this restored car. Earlier SS90 side-valve 70-bhp and later 3½ Litre 125-bhp/acceleration figures are excluded.
cars.summary: The SS100 helped establish the Jaguar name through an overhead-valve six-cylinder sports car combining Harry Weslake cylinder-head development, twin SU carburettors and striking open bodywork. The Jaguar Daimler Heritage Trust preserves ERB 290 as a running example of this early performance identity, making the original 2½ Litre roadster a foundational Jaguar sports-car icon.

cars.variant: Continental GT — original 2003 W12 road launch specification
cars.specification_market: Bentley September 9, 2003 Frankfurt production launch release, reproduced by Automotive Intelligence on September 17. Native 560 PS is retained without recomputing conflicting rounded kW/bhp conventions. Original road coupe only: no early pre-production over-500-bhp estimate, Speed, Supersports, GTC, V8, GT3 racer or later generation equipment.
cars.summary: The original Continental GT redefined Bentley as a modern high-performance grand-tourer manufacturer. Its compact twin-turbo W12, four-wheel drive, six-speed transmission and pillarless four-seat body combined substantial performance with everyday touring use, while the model became the catalyst for the marque’s twenty-first-century revival.

cars.variant: 500 K Special Roadster — original 1934–1936 road specification
cars.specification_market: Original W29 500 K Special Roadster road family, introduced October 1934, produced through 1936; this record does not assign a chassis number or authenticate a particular surviving body. March 22, 2016 factory Techno Classica release page 6 specifically supplies the Special Roadster engine, displacement, two output conditions and maximum speed. Adjacent Cabriolet B details, 540 K displacement, racing tunes and conflicting production counts are excluded.
cars.summary: The 500 K Special Roadster is a landmark of Mercedes-Benz performance engineering and Sindelfingen coachbuilding. Friedrich Geiger’s sweeping body was paired with a driver-engaged Roots-supercharged engine and advanced independent-wheel suspension, creating one of the defining sporting grand tourers of the 1930s.

cars.specification_market: Gooding Christie’s Rétromobile Paris lot 17: 1963 chassis 4837 GT, engine 4837. Auction/consignor report states Ferrari Classiche certification and restoration in 2017 with original chassis, engine and gearbox. This is an auction-documented road reference, not independent factory certification or proof of pictured-car identity. English BHP/French ch output notation, questionable copied acceleration, top speed and conflicting production totals are omitted. No SWB/GTO race specification is inherited.
cars.summary: The 250 GT Lusso is a defining Enzo-era Ferrari road grand tourer, combining Pininfarina’s sculpted berlinetta design with Scaglietti construction and the Colombo-family V12 tradition. Its refined road-car identity and enduring design significance distinguish it from the archive’s competition-derived 250 GTO, rather than adding another year or cosmetic version of that car.
